item.title: Donovan Jackson out with torn meniscus, Christian Darrisaw in concussion protocol
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Vikings remain undefeated at 4-0, but they will have to deal with some injuries along their offensive line.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings remain undefeated at 4-0, but they will have to deal with some injuries along their offensive line.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters in his Monday press conference that left guard Donovan Jackson suffered a torn meniscus and will likely miss the rest of the regular season.

Jackson is set to undergo surgery to repair the injury.

O'Connell also noted that left tackle Christian Darrisaw is in the concussion protocol after Sunday's win over Miami.

But tight end Ben Yurosek and offensive lineman Michael Jurgens are set to return to practice this week. Both players are currying on injured reserve.

The Vikings will be on the road to play the Saints on Sunday.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: Efton Chism III has earned more opportunities
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, OBJ met EC3.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, OBJ met EC3. And the stellar, game-winning catch made by Patriots receiver Efton Chism III will result in more chances to make more next-level grabs.

"Sure, of course," coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Monday regarding whether Chism has earned more opportunities. "That's what happens. I mean, guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities. I mean, we've been finding ways to work Chis in there previously. And it's a balance, but he certainly did a lot of things well. I know that he'll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots."

On Sunday, Chism was on the field for 34 offensive snaps. Targeted four times, he had two catches for 42 yards, including the 23-yard clincher.

In Week 1 against the Seahawks, Chism was inactive. In Week 2 vs. the Steelers, Chism had 10 snaps; he was targeted once, for minus-2 yards. In Week 3 at the Jaguars, Chism had 16 snaps. He had one catch on two targets, for one yard.

So he has already been earning more work, one game at a time. And it looks like Chism will get even more.

Which means that, contrary to the prediction from Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, we probably will hear from him again.

item.title: All five 0-3 teams fell to 0-4
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday started with five 0-3 teams in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday started with five 0-3 teams in the NFL. It will end with five 0-4 teams in the NFL.

Each of the winless teams lost again on Sunday — the Dolphins, the Titans, the Texans, the Chargers, and the Buccaneers.

Only one team has ever recovered from 0-4 to make the playoffs. The Chargers did it in 1992.

The good news is that one of the 0-4 teams is destined to not fall to 0-5. The Titans host the Texans next weekend, in the Something's Gotta Give Bowl.

It's a deep hole, for all five winless teams. It helps to have a 17th game and seven playoff spots per conference.

For the Chargers and Texans, it's a stunning slide. Both made the playoffs last year, and both were expected to do it again.

They still could. Getting that first win would be nice.

item.title: Another defendant in Terrion Arnold case pleads guilty, agrees to testify
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave, as he faces eight felony counts arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave, as he faces eight felony counts arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping. A Monday development won't make it any easier for Arnold to defeat the charges.

Multiple defendants in the case have previously pleaded guilty and agreed to testify against the remaining defendants. Via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press, Boakai Hilton pleaded guilty on Monday.

Under the deal, which results in a 10-year prison term for Hilton, he agreed to testify against Arnold, a first-round pick of the Lions in 2024.

A July article regarding the incident characterized Hilton, 23, as a "childhood friend" of Arnold's. Hilton also was the alleged mastermind of the effort to confront the men who were suspected of stealing cash and other property from a house that had been rented by Arnold in Florida.

From the moment the news of the initial arrests emerged in February, it seemed obvious that prosecutors would attempt to leverage guilty pleas into evidence against Arnold. With Hilton pleading guilty and agreeing to testify, the prosecution may have everything it needs to make a compelling case against Arnold.

item.title: Tests confirm Packers LB Edgerrin Cooper tore his Achilles
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper's season is over.
item.content:encoded:
Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper's season is over.

Head coach Matt LaFleur said after Sunday's win over the Buccaneers that the team believed Cooper tore his Achilles during the game and multiple reports on Monday say that further tests confirmed that is the case.

Cooper was having a big day before the injury knocked him out. He had nine tackles, an interception and a sack to help the Packers to a 17-14 victory that evened their record at 2-2. He had 21 tackles and two sacks in the first three weeks of the season.

The Packers will have to adjust to Cooper's absence while their defense continues to wait for defensive end Micah Parsons to make his 2026 debut.

item.title: CBS reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala heard no profanity from Trey McBride
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On any given Sunday of NFL games, expect the unexpected.
item.content:encoded:
On any given Sunday of NFL games, expect the unexpected.

Week 4 resulted in an unexpected exchange between line judge Jeff Seeman and Cardinals tight end Trey McBride.

It happened after a non-call of pass interference late in the Cardinals-Giants game. It looked like a fairly clear foul. McBride made his case to Seeman. And while the cameras and microphones captured nothing McBride said, a CBS camera on the sidelines showed Seeman apparently saying to McBride, "Fuck you." Twice.

NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter issued a statement calling Seeman's behavior "unacceptable" and expressing hope that the league will hold the officials to the same standard that is applied to the players.

Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing, CBS reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala witnessed the interaction. She heard no profanity from McBride.

“I was standing right there,” Kinkhabwala said on Twitter. “What’s wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying ‘please’ when pleading his case for a PI flag. He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, ‘You’re ruining the game.'”

It was a bad call, to be sure. The latest in a recent epidemic of erroneous calls and non-calls of pass interference. The point is that, as players, coaches, and officials interact after such decisions are made, certain lines shouldn't be crossed.

If McBride had said to Seeman what Seeman apparently said to McBride, there surely would have been consequences. During the Fail Mary misadventure of 2012, the NFL issued multiple fines to coaches for their conduct toward replacement officials.

The league has said it will review the situation. There's not much that needs to be reviewed, however. The eye in the sky doesn't lie, and it doesn't take extensive lip-reading skills to understand what Seeman said to McBride.

item.title: Marcus Mariota suffered MCL sprain on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: If Jayden Daniels is not ready to play in Week 5, rookie Athan Kaliakmanis may get more playing time.
item.content:encoded:
If Jayden Daniels is not ready to play in Week 5, rookie Athan Kaliakmanis may get more playing time.

According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, quarterback Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL sprain during Sunday’s loss to the Colts.

Mariota previously suffered an MCL sprain during the preseason.

Mariota went down during the first quarter of Sunday’s game in London and was not able to return. That came after Mariota was able to beat the defending-champion Seahawks in Week 3. In his three appearances with two starts this season, Mariota has completed 64.7 percent of his passes for 340 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.

Kaliakmanis completed 15-of-33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception on Sunday.

As PFT reported on Sunday night, the Commanders are hopeful that Daniels will be able to play in Sunday’s game against the Giants. But practice participation will be a key factor in Daniels’ return from a dislocated left elbow. Daniels was limited in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday last week.

item.title: Report: Rashawn Slater believed to have a high-ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Chargers saw left tackle Rashawn Slater get hurt in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks and the 0-4 team is reportedly set to be without him for a while.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers saw left tackle Rashawn Slater get hurt in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks and the 0-4 team is reportedly set to be without him for a while.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the belief is that Slater suffered a high-ankle sprain. He'll have an MRI to confirm that diagnosis and he will likely miss multiple weeks if the team gets that confirmation.

Slater missed all of the 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon and he missed most of the 2022 season with a torn biceps, so the Chargers have experience playing without him.

They were also missing right tackle Joe Alt for most of last season and Alt suffered a neck injury on Sunday, so climbing out of the early hole they've dug themselves this season is not shaping up to be an easy task.

item.title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start Week 5 vs. Packers
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?"
item.content:encoded:
Ben Johnson isn't going to play the, "Who's going to start?" game this week.

In a radio interview with ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, Johnson said Tyson Bagent will start at quarterback in the team's Week 5 matchup with the Packers.

"Tyson will be the guy," Johnson said, via Kevin Fishbain of TheAthletic.com. "We'll go from there. We're in good shape."

Bagent technically was not the starter on Sunday, as Case Keenum took the first snap in a cheeky move from Johnson. But it was Bagent’s show the rest of the way, as he completed 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards with an interception.

Caleb Williams is dealing with a hamstring injury suffered during the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. He has been considered week-to-week.

In 14 career games with five starts, Bagent has completed 67.2 percent of his passes for 1,239 yards with three touchdowns and seven interceptions.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary.
item.content:encoded:
After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys, help is on the way for Pittsburgh’s secondary.

Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the Steelers are signing cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting off of the Buccaneers’ practice squad.

Murphy-Bunting, 29, missed the 2025 season with a torn ACL. He had returned to the Buccaneers after he was released by the Cardinals at roster cuts in August.

A second-round pick in 2019, Murphy-Bunting has appeared in 82 career games with 65 starts. In 2024, he registered 52 total tackles with three interceptions, five passes defensed, and two forced fumbles in 15 games for the Cardinals.

He has 34 career passes defensed with 11 career interceptions.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup.
item.content:encoded:
49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk had to leave Sunday's win over the Broncos with a knee injury, but early indications are that he will avoid a long absence from the lineup.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Juszczyk's ACL and other ligaments appeared to be intact. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that initial tests showed that Juszczyk hyperextended his knee and that he is expected to miss a couple of weeks, but still needs to have an MRI to confirm that belief.

Any missed time for Juszczyk would force Shanahan and the 49ers to alter some offensive plans, but they've become adept at that this year and in past years due to an extended run of injuries across the roster.

Juszczyk had two catches for 28 yards Sunday and he has four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown this season.

item.title: Klint Kubiak on taking made FG off the board: I don't regret it, I regret not getting a first down
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: In the third quarter of Las Vegas’ matchup against Kansas City on Sunday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak made a choice.
item.content:encoded:
In the third quarter of Las Vegas’ matchup against Kansas City on Sunday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak made a choice.

Matt Gay had sent a 41-yard field goal through the uprights, making the score 16-10, Las Vegas. But the Chiefs had lined up with too many players on one side of the ball for an illegal formation.

So, Kubiak elected to accept the penalty and go for it on fourth-and-2 from Kansas City’s 18.

But the problem was the Raiders didn’t convert, as Kirk Cousins’ pass to Ashton Jeanty was broken up and fell incomplete.

While the Raiders ended up losing 30-27, that choice to take three points off the board was far from the only reason for the ultimate result.

“[O]bviously, there's a point there where I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game,” Kubiak said postgame. “I don't regret it. I regret not getting it.”

Kubiak later reiterated that he knew “we were going to be aggressive, and that was part of the game plan.”

The Raiders have played well to get to their 3-1 record on the season, and Kubiak has made some strong coaching choices. Even if this choice didn’t work out, it doesn’t mean that Kubiak should change his process moving forward.

item.title: Win over Eagles was Matthew Stafford's 40th career fourth-quarter comeback
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Rams were losing 20-10 to the Eagles in the fourth quarter on Sunday, but anyone who thought the game was over hasn't been watching Matthew Stafford over the years.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams were losing 20-10 to the Eagles in the fourth quarter on Sunday, but anyone who thought the game was over hasn't been watching Matthew Stafford over the years.

Stafford engineered a 10-play, 98-yard touchdown drive and followed that with a 10-play, 79-yard touchdown drive, and the Rams beat the Eagles 24-20. It was the 40th fourth-quarter comeback of Stafford's career, and he said after the game that he and his teammates never doubted that they could pull it out.

"If you don't have belief, then what are we doing? That's what we put all this work in for," Stafford said. "We put all the work in Monday through Saturday so that when those instances come up on Sunday, we believe in each other. We understand, this guy has put the work in to do what we do. Not every game is going to go exactly how you want it, sometimes you're going to have to find ways to win football games and that's what we did today. I know I believe in everybody in that huddle."

The only other players in NFL history with 40 fourth-quarter comebacks are Tom Brady with 46, Peyton Manning with 43 and Ben Roethlisberger with 41. Stafford had 31 fourth-quarter comebacks with the Lions, and Sunday was his ninth with the Rams.

Stafford said those are special moments to share with his teammates.

"We'd love to go out there and score every time we touch the ball and stop them three-and-out, and that's just not the case in the NFL," Stafford said. "But coming together as a team, finding a way to figure it out and get a win . . . Just proud of our group, proud of our team."

item.title: Tyreek Hill still has an active Personal Conduct Policy investigation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Hill's looming return could move the case back to the front burner.
item.content:encoded:
Receiver Tyreek Hill could be signing with an NFL team (possibly the Chiefs) very soon. There's an issue beyond the status of his knee that could impact his availability.

Per the NFL, Hill remains under an active Personal Conduct Policy review.

The investigation was sparked by the divorce filing initiated by his wife, Keeta Vaccaro. She has made specific allegations of domestic violence against Hill.

The full details of her contentions came to light in October 2025.

Hill's history complicates the situation. Past incidents, including a 2015 guilty plea to domestic assault and battery by strangulation in an incident involving his then-pregnant girlfriend, could result in an enhanced suspension — if the league finds a Personal Conduct Policy violation in connection with Vaccaro's allegations.

The league rarely provides a timeline for Personal Conduct Policy investigations. The case almost always remains pending until it suddenly isn't.

With Hill not playing, there's less urgency to resolve the situation. If/when he signs with a team, the probe could quickly move back to the front burner.

item.title: Report: Commanders WR Jaylin Lane fractured, dislocated ankle on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The ankle injury that knocked Commanders wide receiver Jaylin Lane out of Sunday's loss to the Colts in Europe is reportedly just as severe as it appeared to be on the field.
item.content:encoded:
The ankle injury that knocked Commanders wide receiver Jaylin Lane out of Sunday's loss to the Colts in Europe is reportedly just as severe as it appeared to be on the field.

Lane was carted off the field and ruled out almost immediately after being injured while returning a punt in the third quarter. Lane remained in London on Sunday night for further evaluation and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that he sustained both a fracture and a dislocation.

Those injuries have been stabilized and Lane is having more tests done before he will return to the United States. The injury is likely a season-ending one for the 2025 fourth-round pick.

Lane had two catches for 25 yards, but was playing a bigger role in the return game. He returned a pair of punts for touchdowns as a rookie, but it looks like he will have to wait until 2027 for a shot at adding to that total.

item.title: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles could be running out of time to turn things around
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Buccaneers started the 2025 season at 6-2.
item.content:encoded:
The Buccaneers started the 2025 season at 6-2. Since then, they're now 2-11.

Sunday's 17-14 loss to the Packers has dropped the Bucs to 0-4. After the game, coach Todd Bowles was asked whether he's the right coach to lead the Buccaneers moving forward, and what he can do to change the recent trend.

"I'm the head coach," Bowles told reporters. "I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame on that."

He was then again asked what he can do to change things.

"We're gonna fight, we're gonna stick together, and we're gonna figure this thing out, and I'll lead them to that," Bowles said. "That's my job."

The good news is that every loss in 2026 has come in a one-score game. The bad news is they've won none of them.

"We know what the problem is," Bowles said. "It's on us. We can't keep getting close to not winning. That's not good enough. Our record says what we are. We're 0-and-4, until we acknowledge that and we correct our own mistakes, you know, it's gonna keep happening. We talked about it as a team. We're gonna be a team, and we got to play tougher in the end and we got to execute the end. And that's the only way you can win the ball game."

It won't get any easier on Thursday night, with a short-week trip to Dallas. The Cowboys are not easy to beat at home, and Tampa Bay will have an undrafted rookie at quarterback against Dak Prescott and company.

Then comes the mini-bye, which provides an opportunity for the Bucs to make a coaching change.

There's a benefit to an in-season termination; it gives the team a longer runway to search for the next coach. Working in Bowles's benefit is the fact that there's no clear candidate on his staff to serve as the interim head coach. There's no defensive coordinator. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson is in his first year with the team, after being fired by the Falcons. The special-teams coordinator is Danny Smith.

The Bucs could go outside the organization for an interim hire, like the Colts did in 2022 when Jeff Saturday replaced Frank Reich. Or the Bucs could just ride it out, quietly planning for a new direction in 2027 while allowing the balance of 2026 to play itself out.

However it goes, it's not going well in Tampa. After playing the Cowboys, the Bucs face the Steelers, Panthers, Falcons, and Bears before the Week 10 bye. For now, they need to start digging out of the early-season hole. And they'll need to get used to plenty of empty seats for the six remaining home games — unless those otherwise empty seats are filled by fans of the visiting team.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: Jets history will get brought up, we can't think about it in locker room
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets opened the season with an easy win over the Titans, but the last three weeks have not been as pleasant for Aaron Glenn's club.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets opened the season with an easy win over the Titans, but the last three weeks have not been as pleasant for Aaron Glenn's club.

After blowing a lead in a painful loss against the Packers at home in Week 2, the Jets lost a close game in Detroit and then got dismantled by the Bears in Chicago on Sunday. The three-game losing streak calls to mind dismal Jets seasons of the past and the head coach was asked after Sunday's loss if he's worried about the roof caving in on his team in the weeks to come.

“Well, that's exactly it, we have too many people that want to think about history," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "Inside of that locker room, I want our guys not to think about history, because history is going to be brought up so much. And they get it from the outside, just beating down on history so much. We just have to circle the wagons and not let any of that come inside our locker room. We've been working our butts off to change that. But our guys know because everybody's going to bring history in this. It brings so much negativity to us that we have to continue to be positive on what we've been doing. Improving on things, and then the things that we're not doing good at we have to continue improving that. So that's really the focus for us.”

Browns head coach Todd Monken had a pointed response to those who brought up his team's own tortured history after a Week 1 loss and Cleveland has now rattled off three straight wins. Coincidentally, they're also next up on the Jets' schedule and Glenn will need to get a win in that game if he really wants to put any notions of another lost Jets season to rest.

item.title: Kenneth Walker becomes third player ever to rush for at least 170 twice in first four games
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Kenneth Walker has obviously been a major piece of Kansas City's offense since signing with the team as a free agent this offseason.
item.content:encoded:
Kenneth Walker has obviously been a major piece of Kansas City's offense since signing with the team as a free agent this offseason.

But his performance in Sunday's win has catapulted his 2026 season into the realm of downright historic.

According to NFL Research, Walker became just the third player in NFL history to rush for at least 170 yards twice within his team’s first four games. The other two players to accomplish the feat are Hall of Famers Jim Brown and O.J. Simpson.

Notably, Brown (1958 and 1963) and Simpson (1973 and 1975) both did it twice.

As for Walker, he put up 173 yards rushing in the Week 1 win over Denver and had 179 yards rushing in Sunday’s victory over the Raiders. He also had the league’s longest run of the year so far with his 76-yard scamper in the second half.

Walker leads the NFL with 537 yards rushing, 6.2 yards per carry, and 621 total yards from scrimmage.

While he isn’t No. 1 in carries, he’s close. Baltimore’s Derrick Henry has 89, while Walker has 87.

Walker and the rest of the Chiefs will get a break in the coming days with a Week 5 bye.

item.title: Brock Purdy has thrown 113 passes, and still hasn't been sacked
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put up some impressive numbers this season, including leading the NFL with a 126.2 passer rating and 11 touchdown passes.
item.content:encoded:
49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put up some impressive numbers this season, including leading the NFL with a 126.2 passer rating and 11 touchdown passes. But Purdy's most impressive number may be zero.

That's how many times Purdy has been sacked this season: Despite throwing 113 passes, Purdy still hasn't been sacked.

Every quarterback other than Purdy who has started all four games has been sacked at least five times this season. Purdy is the first quarterback since Peyton Manning with the 2005 Colts to start the first four games of the season and not get sacked in any of them.

Up next for the 49ers is a game in Seattle against the Seahawks, who sacked Purdy three times the last time the teams met. Whether the Seahawks can do what other defenses haven't and sack Purdy will go a long way toward determining who wins the game — and who wins the NFC West.

item.title: NFL reviewing incident between Vikings' Eric Wilson and ref Adrian Hill
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: An odd incident took place during Sunday's Vikings-Dolphins game when referee Adrian Hill got knocked to the ground and then got in the face of Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson.
item.content:encoded:
An odd incident took place during Sunday's Vikings-Dolphins game when referee Adrian Hill got knocked to the ground and then got in the face of Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson.

The NFL is reviewing the matter, according to ESPN.

On the play in question, Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon was blocking Wilson after the play had been blown dead, pushing Wilson into Hill and knocking Hill down. Hill got up, got in Wilson's face, yelled at him and pointed him back to his huddle. Hill did not throw a flag, but many people watching the game thought Hill overreacted by yelling at Wilson.

Wilson said after the game that he thought it was no big deal.

"That was funny, honestly," Wilson said. "I ended up apologizing to him and explained the situation. He was cool about it. He understood what was going on. He just said he didn't want us fighting, me and [Gordon]. He said he was just trying to break us up."

The altercation between Wilson and Hill was one of a few between players and officials on Sunday. Official Jeff Seeman appeared to shout obscenities at Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was flagged for using an obscenity toward an official.

item.title: Drew Rosenhaus: Tyreek Hill could sign with a team this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A return to the Chiefs could be in the cards for the wide receiver.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Tyreek Hill could be back in the NFL very soon.

Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that he plans to begin negotiations with teams about a contract for the wideout. Rosenhaus added that he does not expect it to take a long time for those talks to lead to an agreement.

“I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days,” Rosenhaus said.

One of the teams that Rosenhaus is expected to be talking to is the Chiefs. Word on Sunday was that they have already reached out to show their interest in a reunion with Hill and their urgency to get something done went up when Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle during Sunday's win over the Raiders.

Hill spent his first six seasons with the Chiefs and was a three-time first-team All-Pro while helping the team win the first of three Super Bowls under head coach Andy Reid. He was traded to Miami ahead of the 2022 season, but could be back with the Chiefs in the near future.

item.title: Eagles' offense sputters with 68 net passing yards, 0-12 on third down vs. Rams
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The boo birds flew early and often in Philly on Sunday, thanks to an offense that couldn't get off the ground.
item.content:encoded:
The boo birds flew early and often in Philly on Sunday, thanks to an offense that couldn't get off the ground.

The final tally from Sunday's loss to the Rams: 172 total yards, 68 net yards passing, and 0-for-12 on third down.

Over the last two games, the Eagles have converted only two of 21 third-down opportunities.

After the loss to L.A., Eagles coach Nick Sirianni was asked whether the problems are a result of execution, play-calling, or scheme.

"Obviously, everybody contributed to that," Sirianni told reporters. "Everybody. So, there's execution errors, there's coaching errors. Everybody contributes to it. It's an ultimate team game. You can't sustain drives and do the things that you want. Some of our problems offensively has been [that] we've been behind, but it wasn't quite the same case today where we were in second-and-long and all those different things. It was more we couldn't convert on third down for multiple different reasons. So again, there's always a lot of contributors to that. I need to go watch the tape before I react to anything. But I know when you're 0-for-whatever we were today, everybody has a hand in that. Our job is to figure out what happened and get better from it and not assign blame. That's what we'll be doing."

Injuries had something to do with that. The Eagles didn't have receiver Devonta Smith or tight end Dallas Goedert. Right tackle Lane Johnson was a late scratch. Running back Saquon Barkley injured his hamstring on his only carry of the game.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts didn't blame injuries. Or play-calling. Or scheme.

“Poor execution," he said regarding the offensive effort, particularly in the second half. "Poor execution. Yeah, poor execution.”

He was later asked what he means by "poor execution."

"It's just you're finding your flow collectively as a unit," Hurts said. "I think it comes down to finding a flow, finding a rhythm as a unit, as a group, and going out there and executing at a higher level. We didn't do that today.”

The next chance to do it comes in six days, in London. Against the 3-1 Jaguars.

While the season isn't yet on the brink, it's clear that the Eagles aren't the team they've been in recent seasons. They're currently not dominant. They're currently not elite. They've got the Panthers and the Cowboys after the trip to England, followed by the Commanders and the Giants.

The Eagles need to win at least three of the next five before their Week 10 bye. If they finish the first nine games at 4-5, 3-6, or 2-7, it could be very hard to get back to the playoffs.

Even if they do, the 2026 Eagles don't look like a team that can make a climb up the playoff tree.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr.: I feel like I showed why Cowboys brought me here
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wasn't on the field a lot during Sunday's game against the Texans, but his Cowboys debut was a happy one.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wasn't on the field a lot during Sunday's game against the Texans, but his Cowboys debut was a happy one.

The Cowboys won the game on CeeDee Lamb's late touchdown catch and Porter said it was "a blessing" just to be on the field after sitting out the first three games while he was still with the Steelers. Porter played 24 snaps and was in pass coverage on 19 of those plays. He was only targeted once by Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud, which illustrated one of the reasons why the Cowboys were interested in adding him to their defense.

"I'm a dog at the end of the day, and I want to be out there with the guys," Porter said, via the team's website. So I have to prove why they got me here, and I feel like I did that today."

Porter was only with the Cowboys for a matter of days before Sunday's game and he said his unfamiliarity with the entire defense was the reason he "wasn't really out there too much" in his debut. Porter won't have much time to nail down the missing pieces before Thursday's game against the Buccaneers, but every little bit will help him continue to find his place in Dallas.

item.title: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton dislocated his left ankle in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton dislocated his left ankle in Sunday's victory over the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. Team doctors put the ankle back in place.

Thornton will undergo an MRI and receive a second opinion on Monday.

"That doesn’t look good," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said, via Jared Sapp of SBNation. "He's going to fly back with us, and we'll get further evaluation later."

Thornton didn't seem to realize his ankle was injured until he tried to stand up after a 55-yard catch. He finished with five catches for 111 yards and two touchdowns.

"That's a rough one," Reid said, "especially a guy like Tyquan [who is] a great father, a great husband and all that. Just his attitude. His attitude is unbelievable. He's great for the team and kind of a leader for that group. For that to happen, especially with the year's he's having — he's had a phenomenal year to this point — and on a great play on top of that, it's a tough one to see for all the guys."

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: Justin Herbert had one of the grittiest performances I've seen on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Chargers are 0-4, but the coach has not lost any confidence in his quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw two interceptions and lost a fumble as his team lost another game on Sunday, but head coach Jim Harbaugh remains confident in his quarterback.

Herbert shook off some hard hits and kept fighting, and after falling behind 27-6, the Chargers had three long scoring drives in the second half. The Chargers ultimately lost 30-23 to the Seahawks, falling to 0-4 on the season, but Harbaugh loved seeing Herbert competing until the end.

"It was one of the grittiest performances I've ever been associated with from a quarterback," Harbaugh said. "When I say the fight out of our entire team was good, I think that's epitomized by Justin. There's no player I've ever coached that I respect more, or love the way he competes more, than Justin Herbert."

Harbaugh, who said last month that he thinks Herbert will be remembered as the greatest quarterback of all time, said he remains an enthusiastic backer of Herbert's.

"The grit, the competitiveness, the fight, the skill is what I admire," Harbaugh said of Herbert. "We'll take this team and keep fighting. Keep fighting, keep growing, that's what we're going to do."

Harbaugh acknowledged that the four sacks Herbert took were a problem but said that's on the rest of the team to protect him better.

"The quarterback taking the hits he did, there's nobody I respect more, and protecting him is always at the front of the mind," Harbaugh said.

The Chargers are not a good team right now, but Harbaugh does not believe that's Herbert's fault at all.

item.title: Kenneth Walker runs for 177, two TDs, Chiefs beat Raiders 30-27
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Walker continued his terrific start to the 2026 season with another big performance to help Kansas City improve to 4-0.
item.content:encoded:
At halftime, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told CBS' Tracy Wolfson that his team would win Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

He ended up being wrong, but not for a lack of fight.

Kansas City defeated Las Vegas 30-27 on Sunday with a surge in the fourth quarter.

Kenneth Walker scored a pair of touchdowns within 20 seconds of game time to put the matchup out of reach.

The Raiders had taken a 19-17 lead with 4:53 left in the contest on Matt Gay’s 48-yard field goal. But after that, the Chiefs got in the end zone in large part due to a 55-yard catch from Tyquan Thornton. While Thornton suffered a lower-leg injury on the play and had to be carted off, he set up Walker for a 2-yard touchdown run to give the Chiefs the lead back.

Then Las Vegas fumbled the ensuing kickoff, giving Kansas City the ball back deep in opponent territory. Walker needed just one play to go into the end zone, putting the Chiefs up 30-19 with his 22-yard score.

But that left plenty of time for the Raiders to get a couple more possessions. Kirk Cousins connected with Brock Bowers on a 20-yard touchdown to cut Kansas City’s lead to three. While the onside kick attempt failed, the Raiders got the ball back with no timeouts at their 1-yard line with 1:16 on the clock.

Las Vegas got lucky that a replay review was not instituted after a pass over the middle to Tre Tucker gained 23 yards. The ball hit the ground, but it was ruled a completed pass. Cousins spiked the ball to stop the clock before a review was called for, leaving the Raiders with 10 seconds left at the Kansas City 49.

But on the next play, Cousins’ pass was intercepted by safety Xavier Nwankpa, which effectively ended the game.

Walker has continued to make a significant difference for Kansas City’s offense, finishing with a career-high 177 yards rushing. He also rushed for a career-long 76-yard run, which helped set up a touchdown to Tyquan Thornton earlier in the fourth quarter.

Thornton had an excellent game before he had to exit in an air cast, catching five passes for 111 yards with two TDs.

Mahomes finished the game 15-of-30 for 225 yards with two touchdowns and no picks.

On the other side, Cousins continued his excellent start to the season, finishing 31-of-52 for 365 yards with two touchdowns and no picks. Brock Bowers had six catches for 86 yards with a touchdown and Michael Mayer had eight receptions for 82 yards.

Ashton Jeanty was held to 58 yards on 15 carries while he had six receptions for 68 yards.

With the win, the Chiefs are now 4-0. They will have their bye next week before hosting the Chargers in Week 6.

The Raiders are now 3-1 with a strong start to the 2026 season. They will be on the road in Week 5 to face the Patriots. Las Vegas beat New England on the road last year to start the season — one of just three wins for the club in 2025.

item.title: Vikings are third team start 4-0 while not scoring a TD in multiple games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Vikings have essentially co-opted the slogan of the team that beat Minnesota in its most recent Super Bowl appearance, 50 years ago.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings have essentially co-opted the slogan of the team that beat Minnesota in its most recent Super Bowl appearance, 50 years ago.

Just win, baby.

Whatever it takes. However it looks. Only one stat matters — points scored vs. points allowed.

And the Vikings did it on Sunday against the Dolphins with a quintet of field goals, two weeks after the Vikings won in Chicago with only three field goals.

Via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, the Vikings are now the third team to start 4-0 despite failing to score a touchdown in multiple games.

The first was the 1922 Chicago Cardinals. The second was the 1923 Chicago Cardinals.

There may be more no-touchdown games. The offense continues to underperform.

The good news, if there is any, is that the Vikings gained a season-high 336 yards against Miami. The Vikings hadn't gotten to 250 yards in any of the first three games.

Also, tight end T.J. Hockenson took a knee at the Miami two-yard line when he could have scored. It allowed the Vikings to nail down the victory with three snaps in victory formation to clinch the win.

But he didn't, and the Vikings ultimately had no touchdowns, again. And they won, again.

item.title: The AFC road to L.A. may go through Duval
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovations, the Jaguars will play only six games there in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
As the stadium in Jacksonville undergoes renovations, the Jaguars will play only six games there in 2026. They could end up playing two more in January.

At 3-1 through four games and with wins over the otherwise 3-0 Browns, the 2-1 Patriots, and 2-1 Bengals, the Jaguars are in position to eventually secure the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

They still have six games in the division, where the Colts, Texans, and Titans are a combined 2-10.

The Jaguars play the next two in London, against the injury-riddled Eagles and the disappointing Texans. Some stiff tests remain (at Baltimore, at Chicago, at Dallas), but most of the remaining games are winnable, especially given the current quality of the team.

For now, the Jaguars have the best odds of any team to win its division (-250). The question is whether, among the four AFC division winners, the Jags finish with the best record.

If they do, there could be a pair of postseason games with only 42,000 fans in attendance. Which won't be conducive to maximizing ticket revenues (or crowd noise) for the games, but that's one of the realities of actively renovating a stadium while the team is still playing there.

And it's still far better for the Jaguars than playing in Buffalo or Kansas City or Baltimore or Cleveland or wherever.

The bottom line is this. In their 32nd season in the NFL, the Jaguars may eventually have the best chance they've ever had to get to their first Super Bowl. There's still a lot of football to be played, but it's clear that the Jaguars are an elite team. And their playoff games could be played before an intimate crowd, relative to the capacities of other NFL venues.
